subject: OpalWave - SIG evidence prioritization and technical appendix
messages:
From: Elaine Thorpe <elaine.thorpe@opalwave.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@opalwave.com
Date: 2028-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: OpalWave SIG - initial matrix and ask

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for taking the time on the call this morning. As promised I've attached our prioritized SIG matrix (opalwave_SIG_v3.xlsx) — we've flagged controls we need concrete evidence for during procurement. Two asks to help accelerate our procurement: 

1) Can you confirm a single point of contact for artifact upload and expected SLA for responses (we're aiming to complete the assurance review within 10 business days)?
2) For controls related to key management and telemetry (rows 42-59), can you provide a small technical appendix that explains the runtime keyflow and how you produce audit logs for inference requests? A diagram/file would be ideal.

Helpful if you can also mark which items we can accept a mitigated statement vs must-have raw artifacts.

Attachments: opalwave_SIG_v3.xlsx

Best,
Elaine Thorpe
Senior Security Program Manager
OpalWave Systems
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elaine Thorpe <elaine.thorpe@opalwave.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com, jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2028-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWave SIG - initial matrix and ask

Elaine — thanks, received and reviewed the matrix. Quick answers up front:

- Single POC: Markus Klein (security operations) for technical artifact routing; Kimberly Park (compliance) handles attestation language.
- SLA: We'll aim for a 7 business day turnaround for high-priority controls, 12 business days for lower priority items — will confirm per-control below.

Action plan I propose:
- Step 1: We will map OpalWave priority column to our internal evidence index and mark which items can be satisfied with mitigations (control narrative + config screenshots) vs raw logs/artifacts.
- Step 2: Kimberly and Jonas will prepare a short technical appendix for keyflow and telemetry with a diagram and sample log export.
- Step 3: We'll upload artifacts to the shared Drive link you sent and notify when each control is ready.

I've attached a preliminary control_mapping_priorities.csv (internal) showing our proposed breakouts for rows 42-59.

I will kick off internal owners today. 

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: control_mapping_priorities.csv
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Elaine Thorpe <elaine.thorpe@opalwave.com>
Date: 2028-05-19T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWave SIG - initial matrix and ask

Markus / Jonas — I reviewed the flagged key management controls. Notes and proposed deliverables: 

- For KM-1 (customer-controlled keys for critical artifacts) we can provide:
  * Keyflow diagram (redwood_keyflow-diagram.png) showing separation of control plane and data plane keys
  * KMS config snapshot (redacted) and rotation policy excerpt (text snippet)
  * A sample audit log row showing key usage (redacted identifiers) — acceptable as "raw logs" per OpalWave ask

- For Telemetry-1 (inference request tracing) we can provide:
  * Export of telemetry schema and a short example export (CSV)
  * Statement on retention policy and a pointer to trace storage (internal bucket path)

Questions for Elaine: which of these constitute "must-have artifacts" vs "mitigatable statements" for your procurement team? If you can label the matrix column with M=must-have, T=acceptable with mitigations, we'll triage delivery order.

I'll draft the technical appendix and aim to have the first artifacts uploaded by EOD 2028-05-20.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Thorpe <elaine.thorpe@opalwave.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@opalwave.com
Date: 2028-05-20T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWave SIG - initial matrix and ask

Thanks Kimberly — that looks good. I added a short "M/T" column to the matrix and uploaded as opalwave_SIG_v3.xlsx (v3a) to the Drive. High level priorities: 

- M (must-have): rows 42, 43, 47, 52 
- T (mitigatable): 44, 46, 49, 53

We absolutely need the key usage log sample and the keyflow diagram for procurement legal review. Telemetry exports can be mitigatable but we'd like the schema and retention policy.

Can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week (2028-05-23 or 24) to go through the technical appendix and give our legal team time to review artifacts? Prefer 24th after 12pm PT.

Best,
Elaine
(On behalf of OpalWave Security Team)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Elaine Thorpe <elaine.thorpe@opalwave.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpalWave SIG - initial matrix and ask

Elaine / team — final status update before the walkthrough: 

- Uploaded to Drive (folder link above):
  * redwood_keyflow-diagram.png (high-level key separation + HSM/KMS boundary)
  * control_mapping_priorities.csv (per-control delivery plan)
  * sample_key_usage_log.csv (single redacted row + explanation of fields)
  * technical_appendix_keyflow.pdf (compact 2-page appendix)

- For the must-have items (42, 43, 47, 52) we delivered the requested artifacts. For mitigatable items we'll provide narratives + config screenshots by 2028-05-25.

If OpalWave confirms the 2028-05-24 13:00 PT slot for the walkthrough I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda (15 min appendix walk, 10 min Q&A, 5 min next steps).

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Assurance Manager, Redwood Inference
